title: Keyturn Host Protection Plan: Releasing Accepted Claim Money to a Host
content:
Money accepted on a claim reaches the host through their payout account, and the desk releases it against the claim it belongs to. The money released on a claim is not fixed until every further cost accepted on that claim stands booked as owed to the host. Money is released on a loss only once every other claim opened on that loss carries a withdrawal against it. The release is made against the accepted claim on the Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment it belongs to.

### Situation of use and capability

`release_claim_payment_a6ef5b4d` writes a payment record against the named accepted claim carrying the sum released and the reference the host can quote for it, and reduces the enrolment's balance owed to the host by that sum. The host can afterwards see the payment against the claim, the lower amount owed to them and the reference to quote to their bank.

### How it is invoked

The tool is unlocked and then called by the desk agent, who works out the sum released and passes it in.

### Parameters

- `enrollment_id` — the reference number of the host protection enrolment the claim is made under, read from the enrolment record retrieved for this host.
- `source_claim_id` — the reference number of the accepted claim record the money is released against, read from the claim records standing on that enrolment.
- `payout_account_id` — the reference number of the host payout account the money is sent to, read from the payout account record retrieved for this host.
- `released_payment_amount` — the sum released to the host now, in USD, 2 decimal places, signed, passed as a positive figure rounded half-up to the cent; a payment may be for part of what is owed, and zero is not released.

### Return

A confirmation line in plain text carrying the reference number of the payment record, the claim it is released against, the payout account it was sent to, the sum released in USD to the cent and the enrolment's new balance owed to the host. Receiving that line means the money has left on that reference; no other output is produced.
